text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'fremont-dedpool' node gpu-07 reported repeated thermal hysteresis + BMC resets. Impacting tenant:fremont-core. Severity: P1. Pager: carla_sre.

carla_sre: paging in. seeing spikes in node temp then sudden drop, followed by pcie AERs and kube eviction events. full logs below.

carla_sre: logs snippet:
```
[2025-11-03T14:12:05Z] sensor: GPU temp=83C
[2025-11-03T14:12:06Z] sensor: GPU temp=63C (hysteresis drop)
[2025-11-03T14:12:06Z] kernel: pcie AER: Device 0000:3b:00.0: AER Error detected
[2025-11-03T14:12:12Z] bmc: watchdog reboot triggered
[2025-11-03T14:12:20Z] kubelet: eviction: pod oom_kill? (fremont-core)
```

alice.w: @carla_sre oncall handoff? i have a customer call in 10.

carla_sre: handing off to ben_ops for hardware-level coordination, eli_runtime for routing/fallback, david_support for customer comms.

ben_ops: joining. pulling ipmi/BMC serial logs now. looks like BMC firmware reported thermal_trip then recovered, then immediate PCIe resets. could be sensor board flaky or PSU ripple.

eli_runtime: FYI we already saw a few requests rerouted via routing policy fallback but some long-running streams for fremont-core got cut. migration required.

carla_sre: immediate mitigation plan:
- isolate gpu-07 from scheduling (cordon + drain)
- live-migrate (within pool) active fremont-core workers to warm-standby nodes (tenant isolation)
- if drain stalls due to streaming sessions, apply per-tenant connection proxy to drain traffic gracefully
- escalate to HW vendor for RMA

carla_sre: running drain now: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-07 && kubectl drain node/gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

ben_ops: bmc serial tail shows repeated SENSORS_RESET at ~14:12:06 then 14:12:18. ipmi output: `Sensor 21: GPU_Temp - 83C -> 62C -> 84C` pattern. might be cable or a sensor thermistor intermittency. opening vendor ticket ST-98122.

eli_runtime: starting tenant migrate script to shift fremont-core route weight: 80% -> warm-standby nodes over 30s, then 100% if stable. will enable request-level sticky fallback for in-flight sessions.

eli_runtime: commands:
```bash
redwoodctl routing shift --tenant fremont-core --from node=gpu-07 --to label=pool=fremont-warm --batch 20
redwoodctl proxy update --tenant fremont-core --session-grace 60s
```

david_support: drafting customer notification: short, honest, include mitigation steps and ETA for RMA. asking product for approval but want to send now to Fremont ENG.

fremont-eng: saw degraded latency for some requests ~14:12:20. Not all requests failed but we had a couple streaming sessions drop. We need SLA note and ETA.

carla_sre: reply to customer: we detected thermal hysteresis causing node instability; we are isolating the node and migrating your workloads to dedicated warm standby within pool. ETA for routing cutover: 5-10 minutes. hardware RMA opened. we'll follow with postmortem.

ben_ops: drain progress: pods terminating, 3 pods stuck in Terminating due to stuck gRPC streams. initiating connection-proxy drain: `redwoodctl proxy drain --tenant fremont-core --grace 90s`

eli_runtime: rolling weights now. 60% -> warm-standby applied, monitoring. request latency 99p back to baseline for most paths. streaming session restoration in progress.

carla_sre: note: this is not a spot interruption. instance remained powered; BMC resets and thermal oscillation suggests hardware sensor/PSU instability. vendor will RMA but we treat as hardware-failure mitigation.

ben_ops: vendor ticket ST-98122 created. SR: sensor hysteresis + BMC soft reboot. They asked for: ipmi -v sel, dmesg, and the BMC dump. attaching to ticket.

carla_sre: escalation: schedule physical swap. Ops team on standby: @ben_ops, @alice.w to coordinate handoff at the colo.

alice.w: can take swap window at +2h — need to confirm with colo tech. meanwhile nodes are stable on warm-standby.

david_support: customer message sent (copy):
"Fremont team — we detected transient GPU node instability impacting a subset of streaming sessions for your dedicated pool. Immediate mitigation: we isolated the affected node and migrated your traffic to warm-standby nodes; most traffic is back to normal. Hardware RMA has been opened and a physical replacement is scheduled. We'll follow up with a timeline and post-incident report."

fremont-eng: thanks, appreciate fast routing. plz include any request IDs we can reference.

david_support: added ticket ST-98122 and internal incident ID INC-20251103-15 in message.

carla_sre: post-mitigation checklist:
- confirm evac complete and node cordoned
- mark node out-of-service in inventory (serial ABC1234)
- stash logs and attach to postmortem
- keep routing fallback enabled for 10m to catch stragglers

ben_ops: evac complete. node cordoned and powered down pending replace. inventory updated. attaching SHA256 of logs: `sha256: a3f4...be7` to incident.

eli_runtime: fallback disabled after 10m window, final verification: 5 minute steady state, 99p latency within 5% of baseline.

carla_sre: closing P1 to P2. vendor RMA scheduled for next-day swap. assigning postmortem owner: ben_ops.

david_support: follow-up to customer: we'll send a technical summary and timeline within 24 hours and include mitigation steps you can take if you see residual issues.

fremont-eng: ok. please include whether this could affect future rollouts or model pinning.

carla_sre: quick note to that: no change to model pinning required; routing fallback moved traffic non-destructively. postmortem will cover long-term compensations (e.g., increase warm-standby capacity or sensor-level alerts).

incident-bot: [INCIDENT NOTE] INC-20251103-15: P1 -> P2 (mitigated). Participants: carla_sre, ben_ops, eli_runtime, david_support, alice.w, fremont-eng.

carla_sre: thanks team. I'll start the postmortem timeline and include command history, ipmi/BMC dumps, and the vendor ticket. if anyone has extra logs, drop them here.

ben_ops: adding BMC dump, dmesg, and ipmi sel to the postmortem folder now.

eli_runtime: I'll include the routing policy diffs and traffic graphs.

david_support: I'll draft the external customer timeline for approval.

fremont-eng: thanks all, appreciate the rapid response. keep us posted.
